source: NEXT_GENERATION_ASSIGNMENT_ENGINE.md — parameters the specification's text names or requires, which Appendix A's table does not tabulate
note: Appendix A opens "Not exhaustive; it establishes the required form. **Every** behavioural constant in the implementation MUST appear in a register entry of this shape." Each entry here is required by a named §22.1 rule-5 publish-time validation or by a stated derivation, and cites the section that requires it. None of them is a new mechanism; each is an input a frozen rule already reads.

parameters.name: plan.max_admissible_mission_duration
parameters.description: The region's maximum admissible mission duration. Read by V1: cost.opportunity.value_horizon must exceed plan.commitment_horizon + this. The seeded 600 s is the largest value consistent with the specification's own defaults for the other two (1800 > 900 + 600); it is a placeholder for a measured figure, not a service limit.

parameters.name: observability.input_snapshot_retention
parameters.awaits: storage cost model for pinned round snapshots
parameters.description: How long the pinned round input snapshots are retained. Must be at least observability.full_retention, else a retained Tier A record becomes unreplayable and its explanation unreconstructable.

parameters.name: fleet.agent_count
parameters.awaits: the actual commissioned fleet size; re-derives α[tier] automatically when it changes
parameters.description: N_agents in α[tier] = budget[tier] / (N_agents · missions_per_agent_year). Present so the safety target automatically re-derives when the fleet grows — a target adequate at 500 agents is not adequate at 5 000, and nothing about a hand-set α would have surfaced that.

parameters.name: fleet.missions_per_agent_year
parameters.description: r_missions_per_agent_year. The §14.5 worked example is r_d = 20 missions per agent per day, i.e. 7 300 per year, which composes with the seeded budgets to exactly the α targets the specification states (1e-2, 1e-5, ≈1.1e-7).

parameters.name: shard.max_agents
parameters.description: N_agents in the §3.5 bound-2 inequality N · r · k_txn · t_txn ≤ ρ_max · 3600. The Config Service rejects a shard definition that violates it at publish time.

parameters.name: shard.mission_rate_per_agent_hour
parameters.description: r in the §3.5 bound-2 inequality. The bound is inversely proportional to it: a dense urban shard at r = 20 admits roughly 4 400 agents, not 20 000, so shard size is configured per region against that region's measured r.

parameters.name: shard.txn_per_mission_lifecycle
parameters.description: k_txn — one commit, one settlement release, and a measured ≈0.05 reassignment or recovery transactions per mission. SOFT reservations contribute zero because they are never written, which is why the bound is satisfiable at all.

parameters.name: shard.commit_txn_service_time
parameters.awaits: measured commit-transaction service time against the target Postgres
parameters.description: t_txn — mean commit-transaction service time. Measured, not chosen; its p99 is separately bounded at 20 ms by §20.1.

parameters.name: config.cache_ttl
parameters.requiredBy: the Config Service's own materialised-version cache
parameters.description: TTL of the materialised resolved set mirrored at `config:v:{version}`. Config is cache-read but DB-authoritative: the cache holds no correctness-critical sole copy, so expiry costs a database read and nothing else (§3.3). Registered rather than hard-coded because it is the Config Service's own behavioural constant and the register admits no exceptions.

parameters.name: energy.f_derate
parameters.awaits: vendor-curve validation against measured pack behaviour
parameters.description: The configured conservatism factor on the vendor capacity curve in E_usable. Seeded at 1.0 — no derating beyond the vendor curve — because a fabricated factor is less honest than none, and because it enters the combined-conservatism product that §14.3 caps.

parameters.name: energy.combined_nominal_conservatism

derivation.formula: ∏ of every energy-domain conservatism factor with conservatism.activeInNominal = true

parameters.description: The combined nominal energy conservatism, computed and published by the Config Service so that layered fudge factors cannot compound invisibly. Capped at publish by energy.max_combined_conservatism.

parameters.name: energy.combined_degraded_conservatism

derivation.formula: combined nominal × ∏ of every energy-domain degradation multiplier a mode can activate

parameters.description: The combined degraded energy conservatism. Also capped at publish by energy.max_combined_conservatism — the two products are validated together.
